item.title: Russia’s Ambassador to the U.S. Dies at 66 (주미 러시아 대사, 66세로 별세)
item.description:
Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, who served during a rapprochement between the Kremlin and Washington, has died, the Russian foreign ministry said Wednesday. He was 66.
(크렘린궁과 워싱턴 간의 관계 개선기에 근무했던 주미 러시아 대사 알렉산드르 다르치예프가 별세했다고 러시아 외무부가 수요일 밝혔다. 향년 66세.)

Mr. Darchiev died in Moscow of a “chronic illness,” Maria Zakharova, spokeswoman for the ministry, said in a statement published by Tass, the Russian state news agency.
(러시아 국영 통신사 타스가 보도한 성명에서 외무부 대변인 마리아 자하로바는 다르치예프 씨가 모스크바에서 “만성 질환”으로 사망했다고 말했다.)

“We have lost an outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader, a kind colleague and a mentor,” the ministry said in its statement. It described Mr. Darchiev as a “distinguished expert on the United States” who had “served in one of the most demanding areas of Russian foreign policy.”
(외무부는 성명에서 “우리는 뛰어난 외교관이자 경험 많은 지도자, 다정한 동료이자 멘토를 잃었다”고 밝혔다. 외무부는 다르치예프 씨를 “러시아 외교 정책의 가장 까다로운 분야 중 하나에서 복무한” “미국에 관한 뛰어난 전문가”라고 평가했다.)

Mr. Darchiev had been in the diplomatic service since 1992, and he was appointed as ambassador to the United States by President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia in March 2025.
(다르치예프 씨는 1992년부터 외교관으로 재직했으며, 2025년 3월 블라디미르 V. 푸틴 러시아 대통령에 의해 주미 대사로 임명되었다.)

His appointment came as President Trump sought to broker a cease-fire agreement to halt Russia’s war against Ukraine, which began in 2022. Mr. Darchiev’s term coincided with a thaw in relations between the Kremlin and Washington as U.S. policy shifted from staunch support for Ukraine under the Biden administration to pressure on Kyiv to make a deal with Russia.
(그의 임명은 트럼프 대통령이 2022년에 시작된 러시아의 우크라이나 전쟁을 중단하기 위한 휴전 협정을 중재하려 했던 시기에 이루어졌다. 다르치예프 씨의 임기는 바이든 행정부 아래에서 우크라이나에 대한 확고한 지지에서 키이우에 러시아와의 합의를 압박하는 쪽으로 미국 정책이 전환되면서 크렘린궁과 워싱턴 간의 관계 해빙과 시기를 같이했다.)

In February last year, Mr. Darchiev led a Russian delegation meeting with U.S. officials in Istanbul about the operations of the two nations’ diplomatic missions. At the time he was director of the North Atlantic Department, a section of the Russian foreign ministry that oversees relations with Canada, Ireland, Britain and the United States.
(작년 2월, 다르치예프 씨는 양국 외교 공관 운영에 관해 이스탄불에서 미국 관리들과 회담한 러시아 대표단을 이끌었다. 당시 그는 캐나다, 아일랜드, 영국, 미국과의 관계를 관장하는 러시아 외무부 부서인 북대서양국의 국장이었다.)

“The dialogue on irritants has been ongoing, and certain improvements have been achieved,” Mr. Darchiev said last year in an interview with the Russian newspaper Kommersant in which he discussed frictions between the United States and Russia.
(다르치예프 씨는 미국과 러시아 간의 마찰을 논의한 러시아 신문 코메르산트와의 작년 인터뷰에서 “불만 사항에 관한 대화가 계속되어 왔고, 어느 정도 개선이 이루어졌다”고 말했다.)

But he said the United States was tying discussions on certain issues, like Russian access to seized diplomatic properties in the United States, “with a settlement in Ukraine that suits its interests,” which he objected to.
(그러나 그는 미국이 미국 내에서 압류된 러시아 외교 재산에 대한 러시아의 접근과 같은 특정 사안에 관한 논의를 “자국의 이익에 맞는 우크라이나 문제의 해결과” 연계하고 있다고 말하며 이에 반대했다.)

Talks on ending the war in Ukraine, which had been stalled for much of this year, resumed this week in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, after a push by the Trump administration that began in September. The discussions are not expected to yield fruit anytime soon.
(올해 대부분의 기간 동안 교착 상태에 있던 우크라이나 전쟁 종식을 위한 회담이 9월에 시작된 트럼프 행정부의 추진 이후 이번 주 아랍에미리트 아부다비에서 재개되었다. 이 논의가 조만간 성과를 낼 것으로 예상되지는 않는다.)

It is not clear if Mr. Darchiev was involved in those talks.
(다르치예프 씨가 그 회담에 참여했는지는 분명하지 않다.)

Mr. Darchiev, who was born in 1960, graduated from Moscow State University in 1983. Information about his survivors was not immediately available.
(1960년에 태어난 다르치예프 씨는 1983년 모스크바 국립대학교를 졸업했다. 유족에 관한 정보는 즉시 확인되지 않았다.)

Mr. Darchiev’s appointment to Washington as ambassador to the United States was not his first stint in the country or the region. He served as Russia’s ambassador to Canada from 2014 to 2020 and worked at the Russian Embassy in the United States from 2005 to 2010, according to a biography on the embassy’s website.
(다르치예프 씨가 주미 대사로 워싱턴에 임명된 것은 그가 이 나라나 이 지역에서 처음 근무한 것이 아니었다. 대사관 웹사이트의 약력에 따르면, 그는 2014년부터 2020년까지 주캐나다 러시아 대사로 재직했고 2005년부터 2010년까지 주미 러시아 대사관에서 근무했다.)

In the intervening years, Mr. Darchiev directed the North America Department and, briefly, the foreign ministry’s North Atlantic department, before serving in what proved to be his final role.
(그 사이 다르치예프 씨는 북미국장을 지냈고, 잠시 외무부의 북대서양국장을 지낸 뒤 그의 마지막 역할이 된 직책에서 근무했다.)

item.title: General Strike Ripples Across Spain Weeks Before National Elections (총파업, 전국 선거를 몇 주 앞두고 스페인 전역에 파장)
item.description:
Spanish workers staged a general strike on Wednesday for the first time in 14 years, protesting the rising rents and stagnant wages that have become central issues in the national election to be held this month.
(스페인 노동자들이 수요일 14년 만에 처음으로 총파업을 벌이며, 이번 달 예정된 전국 선거의 핵심 쟁점이 된 치솟는 임대료와 정체된 임금에 항의했다.)

Unions said millions of workers participated in the walkout, while hundreds of thousands of Spaniards joined rallies in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and other cities in the evening.
(노동조합은 수백만 명의 노동자가 파업에 참여했다고 밝혔으며, 저녁에는 수십만 명의 스페인 국민이 마드리드, 바르셀로나, 발렌시아 등 여러 도시에서 집회에 참가했다.)

Early on Wednesday, protesters blocked roads in Madrid, set up picket lines outside major factories in Catalonia and disrupted transportation across Spain.
(수요일 이른 시각, 시위대는 마드리드의 도로를 막고 카탈루냐의 주요 공장 앞에 피켓 라인을 설치했으며 스페인 전역의 교통을 마비시켰다.)

Police officers wielding shields and batons forced hundreds of demonstrators away from the Gran Vía, the central thoroughfare in Madrid, which rally goers had blocked. The anger of protesters in the capital was directed largely at “rentistas” — a Spanish term for people who live off rental income.
(방패와 진압봉을 든 경찰관들은 집회 참가자들이 막아선 마드리드의 중심 대로인 그란 비아에서 수백 명의 시위자를 강제로 몰아냈다. 수도 시위자들의 분노는 주로 "렌티스타" — 임대 소득으로 생활하는 사람들을 가리키는 스페인어 표현 — 를 향했다.)

Later in the day, during a march through central Madrid that drew 120,000 protesters according to the government, demonstrators chanted in a festive mood, “One jump, two jumps, whoever doesn’t jump is a rentista.”
(이날 오후, 정부 집계로 12만 명의 시위자가 모인 마드리드 중심가 행진에서 시위자들은 축제 분위기 속에서 "한 번 뛰어, 두 번 뛰어, 안 뛰는 자는 렌티스타"라고 외쳤다.)

Clashes with the police erupted in Barcelona, where a group of masked protesters broke away from the crowd after the demonstration ended, according to local news media. The group smashed several shop windows, threw pyrotechnic devices at police officers and tried unsuccessfully to storm an Apple Store, the reports said.
(현지 언론에 따르면 바르셀로나에서는 시위가 끝난 뒤 얼굴을 가린 시위자 무리가 군중에서 이탈하면서 경찰과 충돌이 벌어졌다. 이들은 여러 상점의 유리창을 부수고 경찰관들에게 폭죽을 던졌으며 애플 매장을 습격하려 했으나 실패했다고 보도는 전했다.)

The left-wing administration of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called for snap elections early last month, after the eviction in September of María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old tenant in Madrid who became the face of Spain’s housing crisis.
(페드로 산체스 총리의 좌파 정부는 지난달 초 조기 총선을 요청했다. 그 전인 9월, 스페인 주택 위기의 얼굴이 된 마드리드의 87세 세입자 마리아 델 카르멘 아바스칼이 퇴거당한 사건이 있었다.)

Efforts by the government to enact legislation increasing tenants’ rights has failed to pass Parliament, blocked by opposition parties. Mr. Sánchez apparently hopes that frustration over that logjam will improve his chances in the vote, set for Nov. 29.
(세입자의 권리를 확대하는 법안을 제정하려는 정부의 노력은 야당의 반대로 의회를 통과하지 못했다. 산체스 총리는 이 교착에 대한 불만이 11월 29일로 예정된 투표에서 자신의 승산을 높여주기를 바라는 것으로 보인다.)

Mr. Sánchez’s government has been buffeted by damaging headlines over corruption scandals, a migration crisis and a deadly train crash late last month. Polls show that if the election were held today, his party and other left-wing allies would command fewer seats in Parliament than would a group of conservative parties.
(산체스 총리 정부는 부패 스캔들, 이민 위기, 지난달 말의 치명적 열차 사고 등으로 타격을 입은 헤드라인에 시달려 왔다. 여론조사에 따르면 오늘 선거가 치러질 경우 그의 정당과 다른 좌파 동맹은 보수 정당 연합보다 의회에서 더 적은 의석을 확보할 것으로 나타났다.)

The government has expressed support for the strike. “Every right that workers in this country enjoy was won through struggle and strikes,” Pablo Bustinduy, the social rights minister, said on Tuesday.
(정부는 이번 파업에 지지를 표명했다. 파블로 부스틴두이 사회권 장관은 화요일 "이 나라 노동자들이 누리는 모든 권리는 투쟁과 파업을 통해 얻어진 것"이라고 말했다.)

Workers say that low wages have left them increasingly squeezed out of cities, where rents are rising. Spain has a shortage of roughly 750,000 homes, according to the Bank of Spain, a figure projected to exceed a million by 2028. Over the past decade, rents in Spain have soared 87 percent, while wages have increased only 28 percent, according to El País, a center-left newspaper.
(노동자들은 낮은 임금 때문에 임대료가 오르는 도시에서 점점 밀려나고 있다고 말한다. 스페인 중앙은행에 따르면 스페인은 약 75만 채의 주택이 부족하며, 이 수치는 2028년까지 100만 채를 넘을 것으로 전망된다. 중도좌파 신문 엘 파이스에 따르면 지난 10년간 스페인의 임대료는 87퍼센트 급등한 반면 임금은 28퍼센트만 올랐다.)

One of the unions that organized the strike on Wednesday, Comisiones Obreras, called the industrial action “a resounding success” that showed solidarity with young workers. But the main employers’ associations disputed the union’s estimates, saying that less than 5 percent of workers had participated in the walkout.
(수요일 파업을 조직한 노동조합 중 하나인 코미시오네스 오브레라스는 이번 산업 행동이 젊은 노동자들과의 연대를 보여준 "대성공"이라고 평가했다. 그러나 주요 사용자 단체들은 노조의 추정치에 이의를 제기하며 노동자의 5퍼센트 미만이 파업에 참여했다고 밝혔다.)

“In short, a failure,” they said in a statement.
(이들은 성명에서 "요컨대 실패"라고 말했다.)

A strike supported by a sitting government is somewhat unusual, a point not lost on parties opposing Mr. Sánchez’s bid for re-election. Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of the conservative Popular Party, said that the strike amounted to a campaign event against a potential right-wing government.
(현직 정부가 지지하는 파업은 다소 이례적인 일이며, 산체스 총리의 재선 도전에 반대하는 정당들도 이를 간과하지 않았다. 보수 국민당의 알베르토 누녜스 페이호오 대표는 이번 파업이 잠재적 우파 정부에 반대하는 선거 운동에 해당한다고 말했다.)

“It’s absurd,” he said on Monday, “a general strike against the opposition.”
(그는 월요일 "야당에 반대하는 총파업이라니, 이는 터무니없다"고 말했다.)

Unions said the walkout was directed at local and national governments regardless of their political affiliation. “We don’t distinguish,” Valeria Racu, a spokeswoman for a tenants’ union, told the Spanish public broadcaster on Wednesday.
(노조는 이번 파업이 정치적 성향과 무관하게 지방 및 중앙 정부를 겨냥한 것이라고 밝혔다. 세입자 노조 대변인 발레리아 라쿠는 수요일 스페인 공영 방송에 "우리는 구분하지 않는다"고 말했다.)

“We have no patience left,” she added. “The power is in the streets.”
(그녀는 "우리에게 남은 인내심은 없다"며 "권력은 거리에 있다"고 덧붙였다.)

item.title: Seeking to Broaden Ukraine Talks, U.S. Urges Russia to Include Europe (寻求扩大乌克兰谈判范围，美国敦促俄罗斯让欧洲参与)
item.description:
The first round of Ukraine peace talks in nine months ended in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday without a Russian agreement to include Europe in negotiations that have extended, at Moscow’s insistence, to questions of huge consequence for European nations’ security.
(周三，九个月来的首轮乌克兰和平谈判在阿布扎比结束，俄罗斯未同意让欧洲参与谈判，而在莫斯科的坚持下，谈判已扩大到对欧洲国家安全具有重大影响的问题。)

The two days of talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations in the United Arab Emirates were led by President Trump’s envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. On Thursday, the two Americans are scheduled to meet with President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia in Moscow and then with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine in Dublin.
(乌克兰和俄罗斯代表团在阿拉伯联合酋长国进行了为期两天的会谈，由特朗普总统的特使贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·维特科夫主持。周四，这两位美国人计划在莫斯科会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京，然后在都柏林会见乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基。)

The Americans said on Wednesday that they would work to nail down the details of what Mr. Kushner billed as the largest humanitarian swap of the war.
(美国人周三表示，他们将努力敲定库什纳所称的这场战争中最大规模人道主义交换的细节。)

The envoys are also trying to secure agreement from Moscow to widen the talks to include Europeans, after negotiators in Abu Dhabi discussed Russia’s demands to overhaul European security structures.
(特使们还试图争取莫斯科同意扩大谈判范围以纳入欧洲人，此前阿布扎比的谈判代表讨论了俄罗斯提出的全面改革欧洲安全结构的要求。)

Reiterating a longstanding European position, Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, the European Union’s executive arm, said this week that a cease-fire must come before such discussions. That sequencing would avoid negotiating at gunpoint and test Russian compliance with any agreements.
(欧盟执行机构欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩本周重申了欧洲的长期立场，表示必须先实现停火，才能进行此类讨论。这种顺序安排将避免在枪口下谈判，并检验俄罗斯对任何协议的遵守情况。)

But Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff, trying to find a path forward after nearly two years of fruitless peacemaking efforts, are pushing to grant Moscow its wish of negotiating the postwar security posture in Europe alongside discussions about a cease-fire and territory in Ukraine.
(但库什纳和维特科夫在近两年毫无成果的和平努力之后试图找到前进的道路，他们正推动满足莫斯科的愿望，即在讨论乌克兰停火和领土问题的同时，谈判欧洲战后的安全态势。)

“We do believe that as we discuss these other issues, we’ll find a pathway to settle them all at the same time,” Mr. Kushner said. The White House is trying to expand the scope of negotiations to break the deadlock on Ukraine-specific matters.
(“我们确实相信，在我们讨论这些其他问题时，我们会找到一条同时解决所有问题的路径，”库什纳说。白宫正试图扩大谈判范围，以打破在乌克兰具体问题上的僵局。)

Washington believes that the Russians will not agree to anything regarding territory in Ukraine until they understand what the postwar security architecture in Europe will look like.
(华盛顿认为，除非俄罗斯人了解欧洲战后安全架构将是什么样子，否则他们不会同意任何有关乌克兰领土的问题。)

At the outset of the Abu Dhabi negotiations, Mr. Kushner said that the discussions were aimed in part at getting “the Russians to agree to finally allow the Europeans into the meeting to make it a multilateral format, which we believe will be very essential toward making progress.”
(在阿布扎比谈判开始时，库什纳表示，讨论的部分目的是让“俄罗斯人同意最终允许欧洲人进入会议，使其成为多边形式，我们认为这对于取得进展至关重要。”)

Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff will make the case directly to Mr. Putin in Moscow on Thursday.
(库什纳和维特科夫将于周四在莫斯科直接向普京陈述这一主张。)

The Russian leader has made clear that his war is about far more than Ukraine. Nearly five years ago, in the run-up to the invasion, Russia demanded a dramatic rollback of American power in Europe. NATO infrastructure and troop rotations were encroaching on Russia, Moscow argued, and should be confined to countries that joined the U.S.-led alliance before 1997.
(这位俄罗斯领导人已明确表示，他的战争远不止关乎乌克兰。近五年前，在入侵前夕，俄罗斯要求大幅缩减美国在欧洲的力量。莫斯科认为，北约的基础设施和部队轮换正在侵犯俄罗斯，应仅限于1997年之前加入美国主导的联盟的国家。)

Practically speaking, that would mean ending NATO-country troop rotations and pulling the alliance’s infrastructure and weaponry out of the Baltics, Central and Eastern Europe and now Finland and Sweden, which joined NATO after Russia invaded Ukraine. Russia also insisted that Ukraine be barred from joining NATO.
(实际上，这意味着结束北约国家的部队轮换，并将该联盟的基础设施和武器从波罗的海国家、中欧和东欧以及俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后加入北约的芬兰和瑞典撤出。俄罗斯还坚持要求禁止乌克兰加入北约。)

When the war started, the Biden administration and its European allies dismissed any changes to NATO’s posture under pressure from Moscow as unthinkable, but the Trump administration has given Russia’s demands a hearing. It is unclear how closely Russia is sticking to those prewar demands in the current talks.
(战争开始时，拜登政府及其欧洲盟友认为在莫斯科的压力下改变北约态势是不可想象的，但特朗普政府听取了俄罗斯的要求。目前尚不清楚俄罗斯在当前谈判中在多大程度上坚持那些战前要求。)

The Kremlin has lashed out at Europe as the continent has become Ukraine’s staunchest backer in the war and praised the Trump administration for taking a practical approach. In Abu Dhabi, Russian officials continued their swipes at the Europeans.
(克里姆林宫抨击欧洲，因为欧洲大陆已成为乌克兰在战争中最坚定的支持者，同时赞扬特朗普政府采取务实态度。在阿布扎比，俄罗斯官员继续抨击欧洲人。)

“I believe that the moment their conscience awakens, they could potentially become participants in peace negotiations,” Vladimir Medinsky, the former culture minister leading the Russian negotiating team at the talks, told reporters afterward, referring to the Europeans.
(“我相信，当他们的良知觉醒时，他们有可能成为和平谈判的参与者，”率领俄罗斯谈判团队的前文化部长弗拉基米尔·梅金斯基在会后对记者说，他指的是欧洲人。)

Mr. Medinsky told Russian state news after the talks that the goal was “to create a comprehensive security system in Europe that serves as a new, modern-day ‘Yalta and Potsdam.’” He was referring to the meetings during World War II when the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union decided the postwar order of Europe, placing much of it behind the Iron Curtain.
(梅金斯基在会谈后对俄罗斯国家新闻表示，目标是“在欧洲建立一个全面的安全体系，作为新的、现代版的‘雅尔塔和波茨坦’。”他指的是二战期间美国、英国和苏联决定欧洲战后秩序的会议，将欧洲大部分地区置于铁幕之后。)

European officials remain divided on whether they should negotiate directly with Russia — and, if so, who should represent them. Mr. Putin has shown no sign of wanting to end the war: Russia has intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities in an effort to make them unlivable this winter.
(欧洲官员对于是否应直接与俄罗斯谈判——以及如果谈判应由谁代表他们——仍存在分歧。普京没有表现出想要结束战争的迹象：俄罗斯加大了对乌克兰城市的攻击力度，试图让这些城市在今年冬天变得无法居住。)

European leaders have also bristled at any suggestion — like Mr. Medinsky’s — that the United States and Russia might negotiate future security arrangements in Europe and decide the continent’s fate without them.
(欧洲领导人也对任何暗示——如梅金斯基所言——美国和俄罗斯可能在欧洲没有参与的情况下谈判未来的安全安排并决定欧洲大陆命运的说法感到愤怒。)

“An arrangement about the future of Ukraine and of Europe above our heads would not just be unwise,” the Polish foreign minister, Radoslaw Sikorski, said last week. “It is actually impossible.”
(“在我们头顶上安排乌克兰和欧洲的未来不仅不明智，”波兰外长拉多斯瓦夫·西科尔斯基上周说。“这实际上是不可能的。”)

Concerned about the implications, Britain, France, Germany, the European Union and NATO sent officials to Abu Dhabi. They did not meet with the Russians but consulted separately with the Americans and the Ukrainians.
(出于对影响的担忧，英国、法国、德国、欧盟和北约向阿布扎比派出了官员。他们没有与俄罗斯人会面，而是分别与美国人 and 乌克兰人进行了磋商。)

“If they have come here as tourists, let them chat in the hotel lobby bar and discuss their own affairs,” Mr. Medinsky said. “When they bring forward some concrete proposals, we will then consider them.”
(“如果他们是作为游客来的，就让他们在酒店大堂酒吧聊天，讨论他们自己的事务吧，”梅金斯基说。“当他们提出一些具体建议时，我们届时会考虑。”)

Despite such comments, the Kremlin has signaled in recent weeks that it is more amenable to engaging directly with the Europeans. Mr. Putin welcomed a call from the leaders of Finland and Norway last month that some other European leaders denounced as endangering continental unity on Russia.
(尽管有这些言论，克里姆林宫近几周已表示更愿意与欧洲人直接接触。普京上月欢迎了芬兰和挪威领导人的来电，而其他一些欧洲领导人谴责这通电话危及欧洲大陆在俄罗斯问题上的团结。)

Mr. Putin’s foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said in an interview on Russian state television in October that there had been a sense, after the summit last year between Mr. Putin and Mr. Trump in Alaska, that the United States could dictate terms of a peace deal and force Kyiv into an agreement.
(普京的外交政策顾问尤里·乌沙科夫10月在俄罗斯国家电视台的一次采访中表示，在去年普京与特朗普在阿拉斯加举行峰会后，有一种感觉是美国可以主导和平协议的条款并迫使基辅达成协议。)

“But that hasn’t worked out, because it’s not enough to talk only to Kyiv,” Mr. Ushakov said. “One must speak to all of Europe, which completely supports Kyiv, and maybe the position of Europe is of key importance here.”
(“但这没有奏效，因为只与基辅对话是不够的，”乌沙科夫说。“必须与整个欧洲对话，欧洲完全支持基辅，也许欧洲的立场在这里至关重要。”)

Despite hesitancy among some Europeans to engage with Mr. Putin without a clear sign that he is ready to end the war, other Europeans have begun to support direct engagement, particularly as the U.S.-led talks resume after halting in February.
(尽管一些欧洲人对在没有普京明确表示准备结束战争的迹象的情况下与他接触犹豫不决，但其他欧洲人已开始支持直接接触，尤其是在美国主导的谈判在2月中断后恢复之际。)

“We are ready also to reach out as one team to Russian colleagues and make sure that indeed we have the same understanding of what it takes to achieve security and peace for all in Europe,” Emmanuel Bonne, a diplomatic adviser to the French president, said on Wednesday in opening remarks at the meeting between the Europeans, Americans and Ukrainians in Abu Dhabi.
(“我们也准备作为一个团队与俄罗斯同事接触，确保我们确实对实现欧洲所有人安全与和平所需的条件有相同的理解，”法国总统的外交顾问埃马纽埃尔·博纳周三在阿布扎比欧洲人、美国人和乌克兰人会议的开场发言中说。)

Mr. Witkoff, who drew fire for calling Mr. Putin a “humanitarian” in St. Petersburg, Russia, last month after the release of an American detainee, did not speak at the news briefing in Abu Dhabi that followed the talks.
(维特科夫上月在俄罗斯圣彼得堡一名美国被拘留者获释后称普京为“人道主义者”而受到批评，他没有在会谈后的阿布扎比新闻发布会上发言。)

Asked whether it would be helpful for the Europeans to put forward one person to represent them in the talks, Mr. Kushner said that would be remarkable, an allusion to weeks of infighting among Europeans on who such a representative should be.
(当被问及欧洲人推举一人代表他们参加谈判是否有帮助时，库什纳说那将非常了不起，暗指欧洲人数周来就谁应担任这一代表而内斗不休。)

“If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation,” Mr. Kushner joked.
(“如果欧洲能确定一个人代表他们发言，那将比让俄罗斯人让他们参与谈判更大的成就，”库什纳开玩笑说。)

He said that Russia would not get a deal on postwar security without allowing the Europeans to negotiate alongside the Americans, but that there was no trust between Russia and Europe at this point.
(他说，如果不允许欧洲人与美国人一起谈判，俄罗斯就不会达成战后安全协议，但目前俄罗斯与欧洲之间没有信任。)

“We relayed to President Putin directly several times and to his team that the only way to get this done is to have them by our side,” Mr. Kushner said. “And I think that they’re receptive to it.”
(“我们多次直接向普京总统及其团队转达，完成这件事的唯一方式是让他们站在我们这边，”库什纳说。“我认为他们是接受的。”)

Reporting was contributed by Steven Erlanger from Berlin, Oleg Matsnev from Munich, Jeanna Smialek from Brussels, Andrew E. Kramer from Kyiv, Ukraine, and Ismaeel Naar from Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
(史蒂文·厄兰格（柏林）、奥列格·马茨涅夫（慕尼黑）、珍娜·斯米亚莱克（布鲁塞尔）、安德鲁·E·克莱默（乌克兰基辅）和伊斯梅尔·纳阿尔（阿拉伯联合酋长国迪拜）对报道有贡献。)

item.title: U.S. Efforts to Tighten Blockade of Iran Rely on Reluctant Neighbors (이란 봉쇄 강화를 위한 미국의 노력, 소극적인 이웃 국가들에 의존)
item.description:
The first step in the United States’ campaign to economically strangle Iran was a naval blockade of its ports, cutting off Iranian trade by sea. Next came a raft of new sanctions, grounding much of the country’s air transport network.
(미국이 이란을 경제적으로 옥죄기 위한 캠페인의 첫 단계는 이란 항구에 대한 해군 봉쇄로, 해상을 통한 이란의 무역을 차단하는 것이었다. 다음으로는 대규모 신규 제재가 이어져 이란의 항공 운송망 상당 부분이 마비됐다.)

Now, the United States is going after Iran’s last economic artery: its land routes. Only there, Washington has hit upon a problem.
(이제 미국은 이란의 마지막 경제 동맥인 육로를 겨냥하고 있다. 그러나 바로 그 지점에서 워싱턴은 문제에 부딪혔다.)

For weeks, U.S. officials have tried — and failed — to diplomatically pressure Iran’s neighbors into shuttering their border crossings, according to three Iraqi officials and one U.S. official with knowledge of the talks, who requested anonymity to speak candidly.
(이라크 관리 3명과 회담 내용을 잘 아는 미국 관리 1명에 따르면, 미국 관리들은 수 주 동안 이란의 이웃 국가들을 외교적으로 압박해 국경 검문소를 폐쇄하도록 하려 했지만 실패했다. 이들은 솔직한 발언을 위해 익명을 요청했다.)

Those neighboring states, primarily Turkey, Iraq and Pakistan, are increasingly wary and disgruntled by U.S. policies they say could hurt them as much as Tehran.
(주로 튀르키예, 이라크, 파키스탄인 이들 이웃 국가들은 미국의 정책이 테헤란 못지않게 자신들에게도 피해를 줄 수 있다며 점점 더 경계하고 불만을 품고 있다.)

So, on Saturday, the U.S. military joined the effort, announcing Task Force Iron Gate, which it says will work on “preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea.”
(그래서 토요일, 미군이 이 노력에 합류해 '아이언 게이트 태스크포스'를 발표했으며, 이 조직은 "이란의 육상 국경과 카스피해를 넘나드는 첨단 무기 체계, 이중용도 기술, 제재 대상 물자, 불법 수익 흐름의 이동을 방지"하는 작업을 할 것이라고 밝혔다.)

It is unclear how the task force will operate in practice, and it is unusual for such an economic and security campaign to be run by U.S. Central Command, known as Centcom, which oversees military operations in the Middle East.
(이 태스크포스가 실제로 어떻게 운영될지는 불분명하며, 이러한 경제·안보 캠페인이 중동의 군사 작전을 총괄하는 미 중부사령부(Centcom)에 의해 운영되는 것은 이례적이다.)

Former U.S. military officials and analysts say the move was likely aimed at taking advantage of Centcom’s intelligence capabilities and resources, which were already focused on Iran amid the war. Centcom, they said, could sharpen the focus and organization of previously uncoordinated efforts among diplomats, anti-money laundering units and intelligence agencies to clamp down on land routes.
(전직 미군 관리들과 분석가들은 이번 조치가 전쟁 중 이미 이란에 집중돼 있던 중부사령부의 정보 능력과 자원을 활용하려는 의도일 가능성이 크다고 말한다. 이들은 중부사령부가 육로 단속을 위해 외교관, 자금세탁 방지 부서, 정보 기관 간에 이전에는 조율되지 않았던 노력의 초점과 조직력을 강화할 수 있다고 했다.)

For Iraq — one of Iran’s largest cross-border trading partners — the latest U.S. effort could be particularly dangerous. The Iraqis fear unrest among smuggling networks and militants along a rugged, 994-mile border they cannot fully control. Washington has long been aware of Iran’s use of the porous frontier with Iraq to smuggle weapons and money to its militia allies there.
(이란의 최대 국경 무역 파트너 중 하나인 이라크에게 최근의 미국의 노력은 특히 위험할 수 있다. 이라크인들은 완전히 통제할 수 없는 994마일(약 1,600km)에 이르는 험준한 국경을 따라 밀수 네트워크와 무장 세력 사이에서 소요 사태가 일어날까 우려하고 있다. 워싱턴은 이란이 이라크와의 허술한 국경을 이용해 무기와 자금을 현지 민병대 동맹에 밀수해 온 사실을 오래전부터 알고 있었다.)

The task force will consist of 20 civilian and military personnel based in Florida, Centcom said in its statement. An American military official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss operational matters, said they would not conduct military operations, but may instead push neighboring states to use their own militaries to crack down on illicit or sanctioned trade.
(중부사령부는 성명에서 이 태스크포스가 플로리다에 주둔한 민간인 및 군인 20명으로 구성될 것이라고 밝혔다. 작전 사안을 논의하기 위해 익명을 요청한 미군 관리 1명은 이들이 군사 작전을 수행하지는 않지만, 대신 이웃 국가들에게 자국 군대를 동원해 불법 또는 제재 대상 무역을 단속하도록 압박할 수 있다고 말했다.)

The effectiveness of Task Force Iron Gate remains to be seen, but Dana Stroul, the Pentagon’s former top Middle East official in the Biden administration, said it was a “‘Kitchen sink’ strategy.” It will aim, she said, to “squeeze any pressure relief valves the Iranian regime is using to circumvent the sanctions and naval blockade.”
(아이언 게이트 태스크포스의 실효성은 아직 지켜봐야 하지만, 바이든 행정부에서 국방부의 최고 중동 담당 관료를 지낸 데이나 스트롤은 이것이 "'닥치는 대로 다 쓰는' 전략"이라고 말했다. 그녀는 이 전략이 "이란 정권이 제재와 해군 봉쇄를 우회하기 위해 사용하는 모든 압력 배출 밸브를 조여" 막는 것을 목표로 할 것이라고 말했다.)

The U.S. official familiar with the talks with neighboring states said that many had voiced fears of “civil insurrection” if they were to cut off smuggling and trade routes vital to businesses and populations on both sides of the border. The official said that the latest U.S. efforts were stoking resentment among its regional allies.
(이웃 국가들과의 회담을 잘 아는 미국 관리 1명은 많은 국가가 국경 양측의 기업과 주민에게 필수적인 밀수 및 무역 경로를 차단할 경우 "민중 봉기"가 일어날 수 있다는 우려를 표명했다고 말했다. 이 관리는 최근의 미국의 노력이 역내 동맹국들 사이에서 반감을 부추기고 있다고 말했다.)

Many of those countries were already frustrated with Washington for ignoring their pleas not to start a war with Israel against Iran in February, a conflict in which they have suffered economic costs and physical destruction.
(이들 국가 중 다수는 이미 2월에 이란을 상대로 이스라엘과의 전쟁을 시작하지 말아 달라는 자신들의 요청을 워싱턴이 무시한 데 대해 불만을 품고 있었으며, 그 분쟁으로 경제적 비용과 물리적 파괴를 겪었다.)

Yet, for President Trump, tightening the blockade may be the best among bad options to try to end the war.
(그러나 트럼프 대통령에게는 봉쇄를 강화하는 것이 전쟁을 끝내기 위한 여러 나쁜 선택지 중 최선일 수 있다.)

There is still no nuclear deal in place with Iran. And the once freely navigable Strait of Hormuz, vital for oil and gas shipments in the Persian Gulf, is now a dangerous route contested between Iranian and U.S. naval forces.
(이란과의 핵 합의는 아직 체결되지 않았다. 그리고 한때 자유롭게 항행이 가능했고 페르시아만의 석유 및 가스 수송에 필수적인 호르무즈 해협은 이제 이란과 미 해군 사이에서 쟁탈전이 벌어지는 위험한 항로가 됐다.)

After months of stalemate, the Trump administration was widely expected to launch renewed strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. But momentum for that has fizzled as officials took stock of a sweeping Democratic victory that many of them, including Vice President JD Vance, linked to the war’s unpopularity with American voters.
(수개월간의 교착 끝에 트럼프 행정부는 중간선거 이후 이란에 대한 공격을 재개할 것으로 널리 예상됐다. 그러나 민주당의 압승을 평가하면서 그 추진력은 사그라들었는데, JD 밴스 부통령을 비롯한 많은 관리들은 이 압승을 전쟁에 대한 미국 유권자들의 비인기와 연결 지었다.)

The Trump administration is now casting about for other options to pressure Iran to accept a deal more favorable to the United States.
(트럼프 행정부는 이제 이란이 미국에 더 유리한 합의를 받아들이도록 압박할 다른 방안을 물색하고 있다.)

By deepening the blockade, the hope is “it just weakens the system so much from within that there will be implosion,” said Alex Vatanka, a Senior Fellow at the Middle East Institute in Washington. Analysts say U.S. officials are hoping to turn the economic screws until domestic turmoil forces Iran’s clerical rulers to capitulate to U.S. demands, or the government simply collapses.
(워싱턴 중동연구소의 선임 연구원인 알렉스 바탄카는 봉쇄를 심화함으로써 "내부에서 체제가 너무 약해져 붕괴할 것"이라는 희망을 품고 있다고 말했다. 분석가들은 미국 관리들이 이란의 성직자 통치자들이 미국의 요구에 굴복하거나 정부가 그저 붕괴할 때까지 내부 소요가 일어나도록 경제적 압박을 계속 가하기를 바라고 있다고 말한다.)

Since announcing Task Force Iron Gate, administration officials have argued the economic campaign made renewed strikes unnecessary.
(아이언 게이트 태스크포스를 발표한 이후 행정부 관리들은 경제 캠페인 덕분에 공격을 재개할 필요가 없어졌다고 주장해 왔다.)

“The economic pain that is being inflicted on Iran ​right now is extraordinary,” Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, told reporters after a G7 meeting in Paris on Tuesday. “We don’t need to conduct military strikes if we’re achieving the same objective through economic means.”
(마코 루비오 국무장관은 화요일 파리에서 열린 G7 회의 후 기자들에게 "지금 이란에 가해지고 있는 경제적 고통은 엄청나다"며 "경제적 수단으로 같은 목표를 달성하고 있다면 군사 공격을 할 필요가 없다"고 말했다.)

The U.S. naval blockade, analysts say, has effectively cut off Iranian oil exports, the backbone of its economy. Some Iranian officials this summer publicly stated that exports were near zero.
(분석가들은 미 해군 봉쇄가 이란 경제의 중추인 이란의 석유 수출을 사실상 차단했다고 말한다. 일부 이란 관리들은 올여름 수출이 거의 제로에 가깝다고 공개적으로 밝혔다.)

With some 90 percent of Iran’s trade dependent on maritime routes, the blockade was also devastating for Iranians trapped in a spiraling economic crisis.
(이란 무역의 약 90퍼센트가 해상 항로에 의존하고 있어, 봉쇄는 심화하는 경제 위기에 갇힌 이란 국민들에게도 막대한 타격이었다.)

Iran’s leadership, however, has had decades of learning how to develop secret business and smuggling networks to circumvent U.S. economic sanctions and withstand sustained economic pressure.
(그러나 이란 지도부는 수십 년 동안 미국의 경제 제재를 우회하고 지속적인 경제 압박을 견디기 위해 비밀 사업 및 밀수 네트워크를 구축하는 방법을 익혀 왔다.)

The new task force, Mr. Vatanka said, was effectively “a recognition that the Iranians were moving fast to compensate” for their maritime losses through reliance on land routes.
(바탄카는 새 태스크포스가 사실상 "이란인들이 해상에서의 손실을 상쇄하기 위해 육로에 의존하며 빠르게 움직이고 있음을 인정한 것"이라고 말했다.)

Analysts and diplomats say Iraq, Turkey and Pakistan have been the focus of U.S. efforts so far. Turkey has largely refused to change its border policies, they said, while Iraq has struggled to placate both sides.
(분석가들과 외교관들은 지금까지 미국의 노력이 이라크, 튀르키예, 파키스탄에 집중됐다고 말한다. 이들에 따르면 튀르키예는 국경 정책을 바꾸기를 대체로 거부한 반면, 이라크는 양측을 모두 달래느라 고전하고 있다.)

The Iraqi leadership has held weekly talks with U.S. diplomats, including the regional envoy, Thomas Barrack, according to two of the three Iraqi officials, who said Iraq was asked to close all but two of the country’s border crossings with Iran.
(이라크 관리 3명 중 2명에 따르면 이라크 지도부는 역내 특사인 토머스 배럭을 포함한 미국 외교관들과 매주 회담을 가졌으며, 이라크는 이란과의 국경 검문소 중 두 곳만 남기고 모두 폐쇄하라는 요청을 받았다.)

The officials said Iraq had so far refused but, in a gesture to U.S. demands, had temporarily closed one or two crossings — often to huge uproar among its own population.
(이 관리들은 이라크가 지금까지 이를 거부했지만 미국의 요구에 대한 제스처로 한두 곳의 검문소를 일시적으로 폐쇄했으며, 이는 종종 자국민 사이에서 큰 소요를 불러일으켰다고 말했다.)

Publicly, Iraqi officials have said the closures were made to upgrade monitoring and security measures that would help curb money laundering and weapons smuggling at the border.
(공식적으로 이라크 관리들은 폐쇄가 국경에서 자금세탁과 무기 밀수를 억제하는 데 도움이 될 감시 및 보안 조치를 강화하기 위한 것이라고 밝혔다.)

Pakistan, whose official yearly trade with Iran amounts to $3 billion, may have taken an approach similar to Iraq’s, analysts said, as it has opened and closed some of its border crossings with Iran in recent weeks.
(이란과의 공식 연간 무역액이 30억 달러인 파키스탄은 최근 몇 주 동안 이란과의 국경 검문소 일부를 열고 닫았기 때문에 이라크와 유사한 접근을 취했을 수 있다고 분석가들은 말했다.)

Pakistani officials have said those recent border shutdowns were based on security issues, or the implementation of new electronic import processes — a move Iranian officials said was linked to U.S. sanctions on their country.
(파키스탄 관리들은 최근의 국경 폐쇄가 보안 문제나 새로운 전자 수입 절차 시행에 따른 것이라고 밝혔으나, 이란 관리들은 이것이 자국에 대한 미국의 제재와 연관돼 있다고 말했다.)

Peyman Sanandaji, head of the Transportation Commission at the Tehran Chamber of Commerce, told Iran’s Mehr News Agency that “banking restrictions related to Iran” risked “effectively bringing Iranian exports to Pakistan to a halt.”
(테헤란 상공회의소 교통위원회 위원장인 페이만 사난다지는 이란의 메흐르 통신에 "이란과 관련된 은행 제한 조치"로 인해 "이란의 파키스탄 수출이 사실상 중단될 위험"이 있다고 말했다.)

Iran is now moving quickly to exert its own pressure on these countries, telling them not to acquiesce to U.S. demands.
(이란은 이제 이들 국가에 미국의 요구에 응하지 말라고 하며 자체적인 압박을 가하기 위해 빠르게 움직이고 있다.)

“We, too, are continuing to pursue our efforts with neighboring countries and maintain our discussions with them,” said Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, in a speech last month, in which he criticized U.S. efforts to pressure countries to stop trade. “We hope we will succeed.”
(마수드 페제시키안 이란 대통령은 지난달 연설에서 "우리도 이웃 국가들과의 노력을 계속 추진하고 그들과의 논의를 유지하고 있다"며 국가들에 무역 중단을 압박하려는 미국의 노력을 비판했다. 그는 "우리가 성공하기를 바란다"고 말했다.)

Working in the Iranian government’s favor is the presence of powerful regional actors, like China and Russia, that are also still willing to work with it.
(이란 정부에 유리하게 작용하는 것은 중국과 러시아 같은 강력한 역내 행위자들이 여전히 이란과 협력할 의향이 있다는 점이다.)

On Tuesday, Iran’s deputy foreign minister announced he had held a meeting with the Russian ambassador to Iran to discuss “how to counter unilateral U.S. actions, and the so-called Iron Gate plan.”
(화요일, 이란의 외교부 차관은 "미국의 일방적 조치와 소위 아이언 게이트 계획에 어떻게 대응할지"를 논의하기 위해 주이란 러시아 대사와 회담을 가졌다고 발표했다.)

Iran can exert economic leverage over its neighbors, said Ellie Geranmayeh, an Iran expert at the European Council on Foreign Relations. Pakistan, for example, is heavily dependent on Iranian fuel imports, particularly liquid petroleum gas.
(유럽외교협의회의 이란 전문가인 엘리 게란마예는 이란이 이웃 국가들에 경제적 영향력을 행사할 수 있다고 말했다. 예를 들어 파키스탄은 특히 액화석유가스(LPG)를 비롯한 이란산 연료 수입에 크게 의존하고 있다.)

Iraq, meanwhile, relies on Iran for more than a third of its gas, which is used to power its electrical grid. When Tehran has cut off those supplies in recent years — often because of U.S. sanctions that hindered Baghdad’s ability to pay — that has triggered huge power cuts and street protests.
(한편 이라크는 전력망 가동에 사용되는 가스의 3분의 1 이상을 이란에 의존하고 있다. 최근 몇 년간 테헤란이 이러한 공급을 차단했을 때 — 흔히 바그다드의 지불 능력을 저해한 미국의 제재 때문에 — 이는 대규모 정전과 거리 시위를 촉발했다.)

The U.S. midterm election results were seen as such a resounding rebuke to the Iran war that countries in the region may simply choose to ignore U.S. demands, Ms. Geranmayeh said.
(게란마예는 미국 중간선거 결과가 이란 전쟁에 대한 강력한 반대로 여겨졌기 때문에 역내 국가들이 단순히 미국의 요구를 무시하기로 선택할 수도 있다고 말했다.)

“The U.S. is currently an unpredictable and, in some cases, unreliable ally,” she said. “Iran is going to be their neighbor, they know they’re stuck with Iran for life.”
(그녀는 "미국은 현재 예측 불가능하며 경우에 따라 신뢰할 수 없는 동맹국"이라며 "이란은 그들의 이웃이 될 것이고, 그들은 평생 이란과 함께 살아야 한다는 것을 알고 있다"고 말했다.)

Falih Hassan, Sanam Mahoozi and Shirin Hakim contributed reporting
(팔리흐 하산, 사남 마후지, 시린 하킴 기자 기여)

item.title: Indonesia’s Vice President Resigns as a Political Alliance Unravels (인도네시아 부통령 사임, 정치 동맹 균열)
item.description:
The vice president of Indonesia submitted his resignation to Parliament on Thursday, succumbing to a scandal about his academic credentials and injecting new political uncertainty in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
(인도네시아 부통령이 목요일 의회에 사임서를 제출했다. 학력 논란에 굴복한 것으로, 동남아시아 최대 경제국에 새로운 정치적 불확실성이 더해지게 됐다.)

Gibran Rakabuming Raka was elected as Indonesia’s youngest vice president in 2024, in a precipitous rise. He was a symbol of the partnership between his father, the outgoing president, Joko Widodo, and the incoming leader, Prabowo Subianto, that elevated Mr. Prabowo into office.
(기브란 라카부밍 라카는 2024년 인도네시아 최연소 부통령으로 선출되며 급격한 정치적 부상을 이뤘다. 그는 퇴임하는 아버지 조코 위도도 대통령과 새 지도자 프라보워 수비안토 사이의 동반자 관계를 상징했으며, 이 관계가 프라보워를 집권으로 이끌었다.)

“The relationship has clearly fractured,” said Yoes C. Kenawas, a political analyst at the Indonesian Survey Institute. With Mr. Gibran’s departure, “Prabowo is attempting to demonstrate that he has stepped out from Jokowi’s shadow,” he added, referring to the former leader by his nickname.
(인도네시아 여론조사기관의 정치 분석가 요에스 C. 케나와스는 "두 사람의 관계가 분명히 파탄 났다"고 말했다. 그는 기브란의 사퇴로 "프라보워가 조코위의 그늘에서 벗어났음을 보여주려 하고 있다"고 덧붙이며 전직 대통령을 애칭으로 불렀다.)

Initially a political outsider, Mr. Joko came to be seen as a transformative leader of Indonesia. He helped rehabilitate the image of Mr. Prabowo, a former special forces commander who was discharged from the military for his involvement in the abduction and torture of pro-democracy activists under the dictator Suharto. To many, Mr. Prabowo was a reminder of the country’s authoritarian past. But Mr. Joko endorsed Mr. Prabowo as his successor, with Mr. Gibran running on the same ticket.
(처음에는 정치적 아웃사이더였던 조코위는 인도네시아의 변혁적 지도자로 인식되게 됐다. 그는 독재자 수하르토 치하에서 민주화 운동가들을 납치·고문한 데 연루돼 군에서 제대한 전직 특수부대 사령관 프라보워의 이미지를 재건하는 데 일조했다. 많은 이들에게 프라보워는 이 나라의 권위주의적 과거를 떠올리게 하는 존재였다. 그러나 조코위는 프라보워를 자신의 후계자로 지지했고, 기브란은 같은 선거구에 출마했다.)

The alliance between Mr. Joko and Mr. Prabowo was cast as one of political continuity. Many voters had seen Mr. Gibran’s vice presidency as a way for Mr. Joko to continue his political influence.
(조코위와 프라보워의 동맹은 정치적 연속성의 상징으로 비쳐졌다. 많은 유권자는 기브란의 부통령직을 조코위가 정치적 영향력을 이어가는 수단으로 여겼다.)

“From the beginning, Gibran was brought on board solely to serve as a ‘vote-getter,’ rather than as an integral part of a unified leadership team intended to strengthen the performance of the Prabowo administration,” said Titi Anggraini, a lecturer of constitutional law at University of Indonesia.
(인도네시아 대학의 헌법학 강사 티티 앙그라이니는 "처음부터 기브란은 프라보워 행정부의 성과를 강화하기 위한 통합된 지도부의 일원이 아니라, 오로지 '표몰이꾼' 역할을 하기 위해 영입된 것"이라고 말했다.)

Mr. Prabowo’s two years in office have been dominated by his authoritarian tilt and populist policies that have rattled the economy. In recent weeks his approval rating has plummeted, leaving the country in a combustible moment that evokes the ouster of Suharto three decades ago.
(프라보워의 집권 2년은 그의 권위주의적 성향과 경제를 흔든 포퓰리즘 정책이 주를 이뤘다. 최근 몇 주 사이 그의 지지율은 급락해, 30년 전 수하르토 축출을 연상시키는 불안정한 국면에 나라를 빠뜨렸다.)

It was not immediately clear when Mr. Gibran’s resignation would be effective. He is stepping down after mounting calls for impeachment over allegations that he had failed to meet a requirement to run for office — holding the equivalent of a high-school diploma — even though he later earned a university degree.
(기브란의 사임이 언제 발효될지는 즉시 확인되지 않았다. 그는 고등학교 졸업장에 해당하는 자격 요건을 충족하지 못했다는 의혹, 즉 나중에 대학 학위를 취득하기는 했으나 출마 요건을 갖추지 못했다는 의혹으로 탄핵 요구가 거세진 끝에 물러나게 됐다.)

Mr. Gibran has said that he finished grade 12 at a school in Australia. He has faced two cases, one that challenged his high school credentials and another that sought to remove him from office on the grounds that those credentials were illegitimate.
(기브란은 호주의 한 학교에서 12학년을 마쳤다고 밝혀왔다. 그는 고등학교 학력을 문제 삼은 소송과, 그 학력이 부정하다는 이유로 직을 박탈하려는 소송 등 두 건의 사건에 직면했다.)

Last month, the Constitutional Court said that it had found no convincing evidence that Mr. Gibran possessed a foreign diploma equivalent to an Indonesian senior high school certificate. But it noted that it did not have the jurisdiction to unseat him directly.
(지난달 헌법재판소는 기브란이 인도네시아 고등학교 졸업장에 상응하는 외국 학위를 보유했다는 확실한 증거를 찾지 못했다고 밝혔다. 다만 재판소는 그를 직접 파면할 관할권이 없다고 지적했다.)

Two weeks ago, the Supreme Court delivered another blow. It revoked a high school equivalency certificate that was issued to Mr. Gibran by the Education Ministry in 2019. But the justices did not establish that Mr. Gibran had forged a document, centering their ruling instead on administrative compliance.
(2주 전 대법원은 또 다른 타격을 가했다. 대법원은 2019년 교육부가 기브란에게 발급한 고등학교 동등 학력 증명서를 취소했다. 그러나 재판관들은 기브란이 문서를 위조했다고 단정하지 않았고, 행정적 준수 여부에 판결의 초점을 맞췄다.)

Earlier this month, what appeared to be a seismic break in the Jokowi-Prabowo alliance emerged. Several officials, including Mr. Prabowo’s chief of staff, who were seen as close to Mr. Joko, were arrested on charges of wiretapping the president.
(이달 초 조코위-프라보워 동맹에 지진 같은 균열이 생긴 것으로 드러났다. 조코위와 가까운 것으로 여겨지던 프라보워 비서실장을 포함한 여러 관계자가 대통령 도청 혐의로 체포됐다.)

Mr. Joko appeared to cast a conciliatory note on Thursday.
(조코위는 목요일 화해의 메시지를 내비친 것으로 보였다.)

“I have told Gibran that any position one holds is only temporary; positions are fleeting,” he told reporters. “We remain committed to supporting President Prabowo’s administration, especially regarding programs that benefit the broader public.”
(그는 기자들에게 "나는 기브란에게 어떤 직책이든 일시적인 것이며, 자리는 덧없는 것이라고 말했다"고 전했다. 이어 "우리는 특히 더 많은 국민에게 이익이 되는 프로그램과 관련해 프라보워 대통령의 행정부를 지지하는 데 계속 헌신할 것"이라고 말했다.)

The controversy that felled Mr. Gibran has an unusual family parallel.
(기브란을 무너뜨린 이 논란에는 기묘한 가족적 유사점이 있다.)

Mr. Joko has faced claims that he doctored a university certificate to become eligible to run for office. Last week, Mr. Joko, appeared in a Jakarta courtroom to display his original diploma from Gadjah Mada University, seeking to rebut long-running allegations regarding its authenticity.
(조코위는 출마 자격을 갖추기 위해 대학 증명서를 조작했다는 주장에 직면해 왔다. 지난주 조코위는 자카르타 법정에 출석해 가자마다 대학의 원본 졸업장을 공개하며 오랫동안 제기돼 온 진위 의혹을 반박하려 했다.)

The Constitutional Court played a crucial role in Mr. Gibran’s ascendance to the vice presidency. In a 5-4 decision in 2023, it carved out an exception to the minimum age requirement of 40 for presidential and vice-presidential candidates, allowing younger candidates who had held elected regional office to run. Mr. Gibran, now 39, had been the mayor of the city of Surakarta.
(헌법재판소는 기브란이 부통령직에 오르는 데 결정적 역할을 했다. 2023년 5대 4 결정으로 재판소는 대통령 및 부통령 후보의 최소 연령 요건인 40세에 예외를 두어, 지역 선거직을 역임한 젊은 후보의 출마를 허용했다. 현재 39세인 기브란은 수라카르타 시장을 지낸 바 있다.)

The deciding vote was cast by Chief Justice Anwar Usman, who had been appointed by Mr. Joko and later married the president’s sister. Soon after, an ethics panel removed Mr. Anwar from his post, citing a conflict of interest, but it could not overturn the court’s decision.
(결정적 한 표는 조코위가 임명했고 나중에 대통령의 여동생과 결혼한 안와르 우스만 대법원장이 행사했다. 얼마 후 윤리위원회는 이해충돌을 이유로 안와르를 직위에서 해임했으나, 법원의 결정을 뒤집을 수는 없었다.)

item.title: A Sweaty, Muddy Jungle Trek to a Famed World War II Wreck (汗流浃背、泥泞不堪的丛林跋涉，前往著名的二战残骸)
item.description:
Halfway through the morning, I’m being tossed around like a popcorn kernel in the back of a troop carrier playing an eclectic medley of Backstreet Boys and Papua New Guinean jams.
(上午过半，我像爆米花粒一样在后贝隆车里被颠来颠去，车里播放着后街男孩和巴布亚新几内亚音乐的大杂烩。)

We’re traveling along what feels more like a collection of loose rocks, arranged to be roughly vehicle width, than a road. I’ve lost count of the number of river crossings, including one where the water lapped a few inches from the car’s windows. And this is during a dry spell.
(我们行驶的路面与其说是道路，不如说是一堆松散的石头，大致排列成车辆的宽度。我已经数不清过了多少条河，其中一次河水离车窗只有几英寸。而这还是在旱季。)

Our caravan is headed for an unlikely tourist destination deep in the jungle on Bougainville Island, an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea in the Solomon Sea.
(我们的车队正前往一个不太可能的旅游目的地，它位于布干维尔岛丛林深处。布干维尔岛是巴布亚新几内亚在所罗门海中的一个自治区。)

The piecemeal remnants of a Mitsubishi G4M1 — Betty, as the planes were code-named by the Allies in World War II — have remained for some 80 years at the crash site of Japanese Navy Adm. Isoroku Yamamoto. This is the spot where Admiral Yamamoto, mastermind of the Pearl Harbor attack, archvillain to Americans in the war, a respected and memorialized figure to the Japanese, met his end in 1943.
(一架三菱G4M1——二战期间盟军给这种飞机起的代号是“贝蒂”——的残骸碎片，在大日本帝国海军山本五十六大将的坠机地点留存了大约80年。这里正是山本大将——珍珠港事件的策划者、战时美国人心中的大反派、日本人敬仰并纪念的人物——1943年殒命之处。)

Bougainville was occupied by the Japanese in early 1942, in the months after Pearl Harbor, as the Imperial Navy pushed into the South Pacific, with Admiral Yamamoto at the helm. In April 1943, Allied forces intercepted and deciphered Japanese communication on the admiral’s travels, and American P-38 Lightning fighters gunned down his plane over southern Bougainville, a feat the Americans triumphantly dubbed Operation Vengeance.
(1942年初，珍珠港事件后数月，日本帝国海军在山本大将的指挥下向南太平洋推进，占领了布干维尔。1943年4月，盟军截获并破译了关于这位大将行程的日方通信，美国P-38闪电战斗机在布干维尔南部上空击落了他的座机，美国人得意地将这一行动称为“复仇行动”。)

Visiting the relic is not for one faint of heart, time or expense. And yet, war history buffs, Japanese pilgrims, a Chicago hot dog baron and lately, YouTubers, have made the journey, bringing a mix of curiosity, complicated feelings on war and, for many, the desire for bragging rights over going where few have gone.
(参观这处遗迹，对胆小者、时间不充裕或预算有限的人来说都不合适。然而，战争历史爱好者、日本朝圣者、一位芝加哥热狗大亨以及最近的YouTuber们都踏上了这段旅程，带着好奇、对战争的复杂情感，以及对许多人来说，想要炫耀自己去了很少有人去过的地方的渴望。)

So far, my journey has involved a flight to Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea, then a domestic leg to Buka, in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville. From there, it’s a ferry ride across a narrow strait, then four hours by rough, unsealed roads to the coastal town of Arawa. Then, another four hours by even rougher roads, up and over the fog-shrouded Crown Prince Range — to get to the start of the trek into the jungle.
(到目前为止，我的旅程包括飞往巴布亚新几内亚首都莫尔兹比港，然后转国内航班到布干维尔自治区的布卡。从那里乘渡轮穿过一条狭窄的海峡，再在崎岖的未铺砌道路上行驶四小时到达沿海城镇阿拉瓦。然后，在更加崎岖的道路上再行驶四小时，翻越云雾缭绕的王储山脉——才能到达丛林徒步的起点。)

I was in Bougainville with the photographer Matt Abbott to report on the region’s quest for independence, and the lasting legacy of a decade-long civil war that broke out in 1988. On our final day, we made a visit to Admiral Yamamoto’s plane.
(我和摄影师马特·阿博特在布干维尔，报道该地区寻求独立的进程，以及1988年爆发的长达十年内战的持久遗产。在最后一天，我们拜访了山本大将的飞机。)

I was curious why people would go to such lengths to reach the site. I imagined I might encounter Japanese visitors reflecting on their country’s legacy in World War II, or American or Australian tourists who knew of the place through family lore passed down by Allied servicemen.
(我很好奇人们为什么会不辞辛劳地前往那个地方。我想我可能会遇到反思本国二战历史的日本游客，或者通过盟军军人传下的家族故事得知此地的美国或澳大利亚游客。)

As it happened, when I contacted Zhon Bosco Miriona, who runs Bougainville Experience Tours, the group scheduled to make the trip that day was made up of Chinese tourists.
(碰巧的是，当我联系经营布干维尔体验旅行社的佐恩·博斯科·米里奥纳时，那天计划出行的团队是由中国游客组成的。)

So there we were in three cars — seven Chinese visitors, two journalists, a handful of guides and drivers — making our way to the crash site. As I learned on the bumpy ride, members of the group had found each other online, looking for others game to go off the beaten path.
(于是我们就在那里，分乘三辆车——七名中国游客、两名记者、几名导游和司机——前往坠机地点。在颠簸的车程中我了解到，团队成员是在网上互相找到的，都在寻找愿意去人迹罕至之地的同伴。)

They were from wildly different walks of life — a cook, a modeling agent, a tech reviewer, a human resources professional, a banker, a woman on a career hiatus and a chemical engineer. Xiaoyu Xu, the engineer, told me he had been to 110 countries, and was making his way through a list of 330 destinations.
(他们来自截然不同的行业——一名厨师、一名模特经纪人、一名科技评测员、一名人力资源专业人士、一名银行家、一名处于职业间歇期的女性以及一名化学工程师。工程师徐晓宇告诉我，他已经去过110个国家，正在完成一份330个目的地的清单。)

Along the way, we got into a minor standoff with villagers over a Japanese tank along the side of the road. The tourists climbed onto the turret, and people from the surrounding village requested 100 kina, about $22. The group balked, and we got back on the road without paying.
(途中，我们因路边一辆日本坦克与村民发生了小小的对峙。游客们爬上了炮塔，周围村庄的人要求支付100基那，约合22美元。这群人拒绝了，我们没付钱就继续上路了。)

“Yumi flow tasol,” I said back in the car, to the amusement of Luke Raupeto, our guide. The Tok Pisin phrase I’d picked up seemed fitting: Just go with it.
(“Yumi flow tasol，”我在车里说道，逗得我们的向导卢克·劳佩托笑了起来。我学会的这句托克皮辛语似乎很应景：随遇而安吧。)

Around 2 p.m., the cars made an abrupt turn at a small trading hut. We’d arrived at an idyllic village with thatched roofs, lovingly tended flowers and cocoa beans laid out to dry.
(下午2点左右，汽车在一个小 trade 棚屋处急转弯。我们到达了一个田园般的村庄，有茅草屋顶、精心照料的花卉和晾晒的可可豆。)

We had reached Kokopo, a hamlet of a few dozen families, ready to begin the trek.
(我们到达了科科波，一个只有几十户人家的小村庄，准备开始徒步。)

Leading us on the walk was the village chief, Robert Nunu. He said his father was among the people from the village who rushed to the crash site in 1943.
(带领我们步行的是村长罗伯特·努努。他说他的父亲是1943年赶到坠机现场的村民之一。)

In the immediate aftermath of Admiral Yamamoto’s death, the account told in Japan was that he had perished as a dedicated soldier, found seated upright in the wreckage with a white-gloved hand on his sword. Mr. Nunu said his father had told a different story: that villagers had extracted the admiral badly burned, but still alive. He died later that day, he said.
(在山本大将死后不久，日本方面的说法是他作为一名尽职的军人殉职，被发现时端坐在残骸中，戴白手套的手按在军刀上。努努先生说，他的父亲讲述了一个不同的故事：村民们把大将救出来时，他严重烧伤，但还活着。他说，大将当天晚些时候去世了。)

Historical assessments of the Japanese admiral have also grown more complicated in the intervening years, as it became known how strongly he opposed going to war with the United States, and how he foresaw Japan’s eventual fate in the conflict.
(在此后的岁月里，对这位日本海军大将的历史评价也变得更加复杂，因为人们得知他曾强烈反对与美国开战，以及他如何预见到日本在这场冲突中的最终命运。)

Mr. Nunu was shirtless, in teal-colored galoshes with a machete as long as his arm. We would shortly come to see the wisdom of both. Within 10 minutes, we came across a knee-deep stream. I stripped off socks and boots and rolled up my pants, mosquitoes immediately flocking to my shins. At the next crossing, I gave in and waded, muddy stream water filling my boots, squishing and sloshing with each step. Yumi flow tasol.
(努努先生光着膀子，穿着青绿色的胶靴，拿着一把和他手臂一样长的砍刀。我们很快就体会到了这两样东西的明智之处。不到10分钟，我们就遇到了一条齐膝深的小溪。我脱掉袜子和靴子，卷起裤腿，蚊子立刻扑向我的小腿。到了下一个渡口，我放弃了，直接涉水而过，泥泞的溪水灌满靴子，每走一步都发出咕叽咕叽的声响。随遇而安吧。)

A dozen people from Kokopo, including a couple of gleeful children, were along for the trek. We walked through potato fields and among pineapple plants. Our path soon became an overgrown blur of green. Every few steps, one of the villagers equipped with a machete hacked away at a banana leaf or a patch of tall grass.
(科科波的十几个人也加入了徒步，包括几个欢快的孩子。我们穿过马铃薯田和菠萝丛。我们的小路很快变成了一片杂草丛生的绿色模糊地带。每走几步，就有一个带着砍刀的村民砍掉一片香蕉叶或一丛高草。)

None of the villagers, save for Mr. Nunu, wore shoes. One of the two women in the tourist group was in a miniskirt and white sneakers that didn’t stay white for long — the other, the agent, sported an orange crop top. (She finished the trek with no mosquito bites on her stomach. I asked.)
(除了努努先生，村民们都没有穿鞋。游客团里的两名女性中，一位穿着迷你裙和白色运动鞋，鞋子没多久就不白了——另一位是模特经纪人，穿着一件橙色露脐上衣。（她完成徒步时肚子上没有被蚊子叮咬。我问过她。）)

Mr. Xu, the engineer, brought three cameras in a large backpack, an action cam strapped to his chest, and a drone in another bag, which one of the villagers carried. The weight wasn’t too much trouble, he said. He’d been to Mount Everest.
(工程师徐先生在一个大背包里带了三台相机，胸前绑着一台运动相机，另一个包里装着一架无人机，由一名村民背着。他说重量不算太麻烦。他去过珠穆朗玛峰。)

After an hour and a half slogging through the vegetation, we came upon a small, unimpressive pile of metal. Don’t worry, this isn’t all of it, Mr. Raupeto said.
(在植被中跋涉了一个半小时后，我们来到一小堆不起眼的金属前。别担心，这不是全部，劳佩托先生说。)

A minute later, we came to the main attraction: the crumbling fuselage of the plane, the engine that had broken apart and other fragments strewn through a glade surrounded by encroaching jungle.
(一分钟后，我们来到了主要景点：飞机坍塌的机身、已经解体的发动机以及其他碎片散落在一片被不断蔓延的丛林包围的林间空地上。)

Since 1984, the centennial of Admiral Yamamoto’s birth, members of the Yamamoto Admiration Society have been making pilgrimages to the wreck from his birthplace of Nagaoka. They held modest rites of remembrance, with sake and food placed atop a cloth draped over the plane’s remains. Some villagers carried the Japanese visitors piggyback across the streams, recalled Mathias Pihei, who was a regional administrator for the Buin District at the time and facilitated the visits during the 1980s.
(自1984年山本大将诞辰一百周年起，山本崇敬会的成员们就从他的出生地长冈市前来朝圣。他们举行简朴的纪念仪式，将清酒和食物放在覆盖飞机残骸的布上。当时担任布因区地区行政长官并协助了1980年代这些访问的马蒂亚斯·皮黑回忆说，一些村民背着日本访客过溪。)

“Through them I learned a lot about this man, Yamamoto,” said Mr. Pihei, 74. “As soon as we approached the crash site, they would shout, to greet the spirit.”
(“通过他们，我对山本这个人有了很多了解，”74岁的皮黑先生说。“我们一接近坠机地点，他们就会大声呼喊，向亡灵致意。”)

If his spirit was there with us, it didn’t make itself known. The tourists busied themselves taking photos of the aircraft, the engine, the interior of the fuselage, climbing the body to pose by the tail fin. The plane’s severed left wing, with the red sun of the Japanese flag, was missing. It was taken from the site to Nagaoka in the late 1980s, and now sits on display in a museum on Admiral Yamamoto. After about a half-hour, Mr. Raupeto started urging us to begin the trek back.
(如果他的亡灵真的与我们同在，它并没有显现。游客们忙着拍摄飞机、发动机、机身内部，爬到机身上在尾翼旁摆姿势拍照。飞机被切断的左翼——上面有日本国旗的红日——不见了。它在1980年代末从现场被运到长冈，现在陈列在山本大将纪念馆中。大约半小时后，劳佩托先生开始催促我们踏上返程。)

About halfway back, what had been sunny blue skies grew darker and fat droplets of rain started to fall. The villagers hacked off elephant ear fronds to use as umbrellas.
(返程大约一半时，原本晴朗的蓝天变得更暗，大颗的雨滴开始落下。村民们砍下象耳叶当雨伞用。)

Roc He, 37, the tech reviewer, who has a following of more than 200,000 on Bilibili, one of China’s most popular video platforms, said he didn’t think most Chinese people would understand the desire to come to a place like Bougainville. They would say the money would be better spent on education or on children, he said. He had not told his parents about this trip.
(37岁的科技评测员何洛克在中国最受欢迎的视频平台之一哔哩哔哩上拥有超过20万粉丝。他说，他认为大多数中国人不会理解来布干维尔这样地方的愿望。他们会说钱最好花在教育或孩子身上。他没有告诉父母这次旅行。)

As for the admiral and the plane wreckage, he said the Chinese generally had negative views of the Japanese in World War II, and it made him think about how far their war effort had reached.
(至于这位大将和飞机残骸，他说中国人普遍对二战中的日本持负面看法，这让他思考他们的战争努力延伸到了多远。)

I told him having grown up in South Korea myself, the history I was taught was predominantly concerned with the travails of having been colonized by the Japanese and our struggle for independence, and less with the battles far beyond our shores. Not unlike Bougainville, we had been at the mercy of land grabs by outsiders and their contests for dominion, with little heed for the fate of people living in these places.
(我告诉他，我自己在韩国长大，我所学的历史主要关注被日本殖民的苦难和我们争取独立的斗争，而较少涉及远在我们海岸之外的战役。与布干维尔不无相似，我们曾受制于外来者的土地掠夺和他们争夺统治权的角逐，很少顾及生活在这些地方的人的命运。)

It was nearly 6 p.m. by the time we were back at the cars. Vinsa Hu, the agent, had logged the return journey on her Apple Watch — 1.5 hours, 240 calories, 4 meters of elevation, 4.3 kilometers (2.7 miles).
(我们回到车旁时已近下午6点。经纪人胡文萨在她的Apple Watch上记录了返程——1.5小时，240卡路里，4米海拔爬升，4.3公里（2.7英里）。)

Mr. Pihei, the former administrator, said he wished the plane were shielded from the elements so it could stand as a symbol with a message to visitors to Bougainville. The admiral may be associated with Japan’s wartime atrocities for many, but Mr. Pihei said that in the context of Bougainville, still reeling from its own war, the plane could stand for something different.
(前行政长官皮黑先生说，他希望飞机能得到保护免受风吹日晒，这样它就能作为一个象征，向布干维尔的游客传递一个信息。对许多人来说，这位大将可能与日本的战时暴行联系在一起，但皮黑先生说，在仍饱受自身战争创伤的布干维尔背景下，这架飞机可以代表不同的东西。)

“When they see the plane, they see peace, because the person who died in the plane was a man of peace. He did not want war,” Mr. Pihei said. “Bougainville, too, does not war anymore. That plane and Bougainville are one. That’s the way I see it.”
(“当他们看到这架飞机时，他们看到的是和平，因为死在飞机里的人是一个和平之人。他不想战争，”皮黑先生说。“布干维尔也不再战争了。那架飞机和布干维尔是一体的。我就是这么看的。”)

item.title: Journalist’s Arrest Adds to Fears Israeli Security Agency Is Being Politicized (언론인 체포로 이스라엘 보안기관의 정치화 우려 증폭)
item.description:
Abed Abu Shehadeh, a 38-year-old journalist and a Palestinian citizen of Israel, said he was putting on his pajamas on the evening of Nov. 3 when police officers and intelligence agents burst into his family’s third-floor apartment in Jaffa.
(38세 언론인이자 이스라엘 국적의 팔레스타인인인 아베드 아부 셰하데는 11월 3일 저녁 잠옷을 입고 있던 중 경찰관과 정보 요원들이 야파에 있는 가족의 3층 아파트에 들이닥쳤다고 말했다.)

They strip-searched him, confiscated his phone, allowed him to dress and then whisked him away, he said in an interview at a restaurant in the city.
(그는 시내 한 식당에서 가진 인터뷰에서 이들이 자신을 알몸 수색하고 휴대전화를 압수했으며 옷을 입도록 허락한 뒤 재빨리 데려갔다고 말했다.)

Five days later, after interrogations by Israel’s domestic security agency, the Shin Bet, Mr. Abu Shehadeh, who lives with his wife and two young children, was let go.
(5일 후, 이스라엘 국내 보안기관인 신베트의 심문을 받은 뒤 아내와 두 어린 자녀와 함께 사는 아부 셰하데 씨는 석방되었다.)

A former elected member of the Tel Aviv-Jaffa City Council, Mr. Abu Shehadeh has not been charged with a crime. The Israeli authorities have not publicly offered a reason for his arrest, though court records reviewed by The New York Times show that he was accused of being in contact with an unnamed “foreign agent.”
(텔아비브-야파 시의회에서 선출직 의원을 지낸 아부 셰하데 씨는 어떤 범죄로도 기소되지 않았다. 이스라엘 당국은 그의 체포 이유를 공개적으로 밝히지 않았지만, 뉴욕타임스가 검토한 법원 기록에 따르면 그는 이름이 밝혀지지 않은 “외국 요원”과 접촉한 혐의를 받았다.)

His highly publicized arrest — a week after Israel’s national elections — came as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies have claimed that foreign actors illegally funneled large amounts of money to bribe Arab citizens to vote for Arab political parties.
(이스라엘 총선 일주일 후에 이루어진 그의 체포는 크게 보도되었는데, 이는 베냐민 네타냐후 총리와 그의 동맹들이 외국 행위자들이 아랍 시민들에게 아랍 정당에 투표하도록 뇌물을 주기 위해 대규모 자금을 불법적으로 유입했다고 주장해 온 가운데 나온 것이다.)

Critics say that Mr. Netanyahu and his allies are seeking to undermine the legitimacy of the record gains by Arab parties in the Parliament, or the Knesset, by contending without basis that Arab voters stole the election.
(비판론자들은 네타냐후 씨와 그의 동맹들이 아랍 유권자들이 선거를 훔쳤다고 근거 없이 주장함으로써 의회(크네셋)에서 아랍 정당들이 기록적인 의석을 얻은 것의 정당성을 훼손하려 한다고 말한다.)

Mr. Abu Shehadeh’s arrest has intensified warnings from prominent analysts and former security officials that the Israeli security services are overstepping their authority and becoming dangerously politicized in trying to promote the prime minister’s objectives.
(아부 셰하데 씨의 체포는 저명한 분석가들과 전직 보안 관리들이 이스라엘 보안기관이 권한을 넘어 총리의 목표를 추진하려다 위험할 정도로 정치화되고 있다는 경고를 강화시켰다.)

The Shin Bet is “smearing a broad, legitimate segment of citizens fighting for their rights,” Adm. Ami Ayalon, a former director of the security agency, said last week after meeting with its current leadership. He added that the Shin Bet was “failing in its most critical duty: defending the democratic system and its institutions.”
(보안기관 전 국장인 아미 아얄론 예비역 소장은 지난주 현 지도부를 만난 뒤 신베트가 “자신의 권리를 위해 싸우는 광범위하고 정당한 시민층을 매도하고 있다”고 말했다. 그는 신베트가 “가장 중요한 의무인 민주 체제와 그 제도들을 수호하는 일에 실패하고 있다”고 덧붙였다.)

The Shin Bet did not respond to a request for comment. The police did not immediately respond for a request for comment.
(신베트는 논평 요청에 응답하지 않았다. 경찰은 논평 요청에 즉시 응답하지 않았다.)

Arab voters turned out during the election last month in huge numbers, delivering 19 seats in Israel’s Parliament to two Arab parties.
(지난달 선거에서 아랍 유권자들이 대거 투표에 참여해 두 아랍 정당에 이스라엘 의회 의석 19석을 안겼다.)

Mr. Netanyahu and his allies’ share of Knesset seats declined and their path to forming a new governing coalition narrowed. The leader of the anti-Netanyahu opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, is trying to assemble a coalition and could turn to the Arab parties for support.
(네타냐후 씨와 그의 동맹이 차지한 크네셋 의석은 줄었고 새 연립정부를 구성할 수 있는 경로는 좁아졌다. 반네타냐후 야당 지도자인 가디 아이젠코트는 연립정부 구성을 시도하고 있으며 지지를 얻기 위해 아랍 정당들에 손을 내밀 수 있다.)

During a speech on Tuesday in Parliament, Mr. Netanyahu repeated demands to investigate claims that foreign actors influenced the election results and called Arab lawmakers “terror supporters” and “Israel haters.”
(화요일 의회 연설에서 네타냐후 씨는 외국 행위자들이 선거 결과에 영향을 미쳤다는 주장을 조사하라는 요구를 반복하고 아랍 의원들을 “테러 지지자”이자 “이스라엘 혐오자”라고 불렀다.)

Police and intelligence investigators have not publicly shared any evidence to back up the allegations. Last week, Noam Sohlberg, a Supreme Court justice chairing the Central Elections Committee, certified the final vote tally and dismissed attempts to cast doubt on Arab votes.
(경찰과 정보 수사관들은 이러한 주장을 뒷받침할 어떤 증거도 공개적으로 공유하지 않았다. 지난주 중앙선거관리위원회 위원장을 맡은 대법원 판사 노암 졸버그는 최종 투표 집계를 인증하고 아랍인 투표에 의문을 제기하려는 시도를 일축했다.)

A day after his release, Mr. Abu Shehadeh said he was confident that the Israeli authorities would not have arrested him if Arab voter turnout had been lower.
(석방된 다음 날 아부 셰하데 씨는 아랍 유권자 투표율이 더 낮았다면 이스라엘 당국이 자신을 체포하지 않았을 것이라고 확신한다고 말했다.)

“It’s political persecution to delegitimize Arab voters,” he said, while munching on pizza as a steady stream of well-wishers stopped to embrace him.
(그는 피자를 먹으며 끊임없이 이어지는 안부 인사 사람들이 다가와 그를 껴안는 가운데 “아랍 유권자의 정당성을 훼손하려는 정치적 박해”라고 말했다.)

Mr. Abu Shehadeh said that his interrogators centered their questioning on his work as a journalist, specifically a podcast interview he conducted in Qatar last month ahead of the election with Azmi Bishara, a former member of the Israeli Parliament.
(아부 셰하데 씨는 심문관들이 자신의 언론인으로서의 활동, 특히 지난달 선거를 앞두고 카타르에서 전직 이스라엘 의회 의원인 아즈미 비샤라와 진행한 팟캐스트 인터뷰에 질문을 집중했다고 말했다.)

Mr. Bishara, a prominent Arab intellectual now based in Qatar, was accused by Israel in 2007 of spying for Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militant group in Lebanon.
(현재 카타르에 거점을 둔 저명한 아랍 지식인인 비샤라 씨는 2007년 이스라엘로부터 레바논의 이란 지원 무장단체인 헤즈볼라를 위해 스파이 활동을 했다는 혐의를 받았다.)

Mr. Bishara has denied any wrongdoing and said in a statement on Tuesday that he has not returned to Israel since he was accused because he lacks “faith in the fairness of the Israeli judicial system when it comes to security-related charges.”
(비샤라 씨는 어떤 잘못도 부인했으며 화요일 성명에서 “안보 관련 혐의에 관한 한 이스라엘 사법 체제의 공정성에 대한 신뢰”가 부족하기 때문에 혐의를 받은 이후 이스라엘로 돌아오지 않았다고 말했다.)

Mr. Bishara rejected any suggestion he was a “foreign agent” and emphasized that he is a “researcher, writer, and a progressive, liberal democrat.” He said that he granted the interview to Mr. Abu Shehadeh in hopes of sharing his analysis of “the situation with Arab citizens within Israel” and “to help increase voter turnout, which is essential for ousting Netanyahu’s current coalition.”
(비샤라 씨는 자신이 “외국 요원”이라는 어떤 암시도 거부하고 자신이 “연구자이자 작가이며 진보적이고 자유주의적인 민주주의자”임을 강조했다. 그는 “이스라엘 내 아랍 시민들의 상황”에 대한 자신의 분석을 공유하고 “네타냐후 현 연립정부를 축출하는 데 필수적인 투표율을 높이는 데 도움을 주기”를 바라며 아부 셰하데 씨와 인터뷰를 했다고 말했다.)

He added, “I hope my interview has had some impact.”
(그는 “내 인터뷰가 어느 정도 영향력을 발휘했기를 바란다”고 덧붙였다.)

Israeli journalists routinely speak with people that the Israeli government considers adversaries without facing legal consequences. Some have even stayed in contact with Hamas officials, including after the group’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack against Israel.
(이스라엘 언론인들은 이스라엘 정부가 적대시하는 인물들과 일상적으로 대화하며 법적 결과에 직면하지 않는다. 일부는 2023년 10월 7일 하마스의 이스라엘 공격 이후에도 하마스 관리들과 계속 연락을 유지하기도 했다.)

Mr. Abu Shehadeh, who was born in Jaffa, had worked as an auto mechanic until, he said, the murder of a close friend motivated him to finish high school and enroll in university. In 2018, running on the slate of Balad, a Palestinian nationalist party in Israel, he won a seat on the Tel Aviv-Jaffa City Council, where he worked on several initiatives promoting Arab-Jewish understanding.
(야파에서 태어난 아부 셰하데 씨는 자동차 정비사로 일했는데, 그가 말하기를 가까운 친구의 살해가 그를 고등학교를 마치고 대학에 진학하도록 동기를 부여했다고 한다. 2018년 이스라엘의 팔레스타인 민족주의 정당인 발라드의 명부로 출마해 텔아비브-야파 시의회 의석을 얻었으며, 그곳에서 아랍-유대인 이해를 증진하는 여러 계획에 참여했다.)

When violence broke out between Arab and Jewish citizens in some Israeli cities in 2021, Mr. Abu Shehadeh worked with young Arabs to ease the tension.
(2021년 일부 이스라엘 도시에서 아랍인과 유대인 시민 사이에 폭력 사태가 벌어졌을 때 아부 셰하데 씨는 젊은 아랍인들과 함께 긴장을 완화하기 위해 일했다.)

After leaving the City Council, he has worked as a journalist, both as a podcast host for Arab 48, a local news site focusing on Palestinian issues, and as a political commentator on television.
(시의회를 떠난 후 그는 팔레스타인 문제에 초점을 맞춘 지역 뉴스 사이트인 아랍 48의 팟캐스트 진행자이자 텔레비전 정치 논평가로 일해 왔다.)

Mr. Abu Shehadeh said he worried that his detention marked a dangerous turn by the Israel authorities toward persecuting political dissidents. “First they will come for us, the Arabs,” he said. “Then they will come for anyone who opposes the government.”
(아부 셰하데 씨는 자신의 구금이 이스라엘 당국이 정치적 반체제 인사를 박해하는 위험한 전환점을 표시하는 것 같아 걱정된다고 말했다. “먼저 그들은 우리 아랍인들을 찾아올 것입니다. 그다음에는 정부에 반대하는 모든 사람을 찾아올 것입니다”라고 그는 말했다.)

While held last week in a windowless jail cell, Mr. Abu Shehadeh said, he feared he would be locked away for a long time.
(아부 셰하데 씨는 지난주 창문 없는 감방에 갇혀 있는 동안 오랫동안 갇혀 있을까 봐 두려웠다고 말했다.)

Hours after his release on Sunday, he urged more than 100 Jews and Arabs, who had gathered in a community center to welcome him home, to speak out.
(일요일 석방된 지 몇 시간 후, 그는 그를 집으로 맞이하기 위해 한 커뮤니티 센터에 모인 100여 명의 유대인과 아랍인에게 목소리를 내라고 촉구했다.)

“Don’t be fearful,” he told the cheering crowd, saying that history changes for the better when people refuse to be intimidated.
(“두려워하지 마세요”라고 그는 환호하는 군중에게 말하며 사람들이 위협에 굴하지 않을 때 역사가 더 나은 방향으로 바뀐다고 말했다.)

“We are fighting for a better future to both nations,” he said, referring to Israelis and Palestinians, “because that’s the right thing to do.”
(“우리는 이스라엘인과 팔레스타인인 모두에게 더 나은 미래를 위해 싸우고 있습니다. 그것이 옳은 일이기 때문입니다”라고 그는 말했다.)

Ronen Bergman contributed reporting to this article.
(로넨 베르그만이 이 기사에 보도를 기여했습니다.)
